starter.CASES.md:
# Input and self-check cases

| Input or action | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Submit Cedar Trail Outfitters | Cedar Trail Outfitters; Located in: Fairhaven; CEO: Rowan Patel; Products offered: Daypack, Trail Bottle, Rain Shell |
| Submit Sunrise Bakery | Sunrise Bakery; Located in: Mapleton; CEO: Avery Kim; Products offered: Sourdough, Blueberry Muffin, Cinnamon Roll |
| Submit Harbor Books | Harbor Books; Located in: Lakeside; CEO: Morgan Reed; Products offered: Mystery Novel, Nature Guide, Sketchbook |
| Type Cedar and choose its autocomplete suggestion | The name is completed and the Cedar card appears with its local display image. |
| Submit a name with spaces around it | Surrounding spaces are ignored. |
| Submit No Such Business after a successful match | The previous card is hidden; No business found. is shown; no exception. |
| Submit an empty field or only spaces | Same no-match state. |
| Submit cedar trail outfitters | No match; the reference uses exact case-sensitive names. |
| Change a display_image to images/missing.svg and show that business | Image unavailable for followed by the business name; the other details remain usable. |
| Put HTML-looking text in a location/product string | The characters display as text. |
| Select two different businesses repeatedly | One current card and one current image/fallback, without old company details. |

The stock starter remains unfinished until its array and renderBusiness are
completed. For a browser check, complete it with the reference data and rendering,
then add a fourth fictional business and retain the earlier three.

starter.README.md:
# My Favorite Businesses II

Build a searchable business directory using arrays of objects, Materialize
autocomplete and D3 card rendering. This optional project extends My Favorite
Businesses. Its starter and reference are separate saved projects.

Open index.html directly in a browser without a server. The project includes
its libraries and example images; it works offline. Edit script.js.

## Required work

1. Copy at least three business objects from the earlier project. Keep each name,
   location, CEO and products array. Add logo_image and display_image to each.
   The included SVG files can be reused or replaced with local images.
2. Build autocomplete choices from the same array. The shared setup calls
   renderBusiness when a suggestion is chosen or Show business is submitted.
3. Complete renderBusiness. Trim surrounding spaces, find the exact name and
   render one Materialize card using the selected object's fields.
4. For blank/unknown names hide the previous card and show "No business found."
   Render values as text. Show a text fallback when the display image fails.

Materialize's onAutocomplete callback receives the chosen name. Its data option
maps names to logo URLs. D3 .text(value) writes text; .attr(name, null) removes an
attribute. Clear the old image container before inserting a new image so old
load/error events cannot change the new card.

The reference uses fictional Cedar Trail Outfitters, Sunrise Bakery and Harbor
Books. Reference matches are case sensitive; surrounding spaces are ignored.
Selecting a suggestion renders the card immediately. The Show business button
also accepts a typed exact name.

Read CASES.md for concrete inputs and expected results. Complete when all
businesses, autocomplete selection, repeated changes, unknown/blank names and
a broken image pass those checks. Save the project and export its ZIP.

The starter leaves the business array and rendering work unfinished. The
reference demonstrates one complete implementation.
starter.SOURCES.md:
# Sources and adaptation

Original assignment:
https://codepen.io/junilearning/pen/50854534e6dccd9c7bedc0a2d01aded7

Original reference:
https://codepen.io/junilearning/pen/7cbfe6e04babe21bb34a6d6af1028f57

Both complete original panels, all HTML/CSS/JS settings and official exports
were retained and compared on 2026-11-14. The original starter has blank HTML
and CSS and a comment brief. The reference uses Materialize 1.0.0 and D3 6.2.0
to search a three-company array and fill one card.

This local implementation supplies full HTML/CSS scaffolding, local example
images, a deliberately unfinished starter and a separate working reference.
Fictional records replace historical company facts. The no-match and failed-image
branches satisfy the site's existing assignment. The unnecessary legacy
jquery.materialize-autocomplete plug-in is omitted; Materialize's own
M.Autocomplete provides the assigned behavior.

D3 7.9.0 is the existing audited site adaptation, with the same selection/event
API used here. Materialize is the existing pinned 1.0.0 course asset. Libraries
and licenses are included. The original starter export's MIT notice is retained;
the official reference export contained no separate license file. The local
exercise implementation and SVG illustrations are newly authored.

reference.CASES.md:
# Input and self-check cases

| Input or action | Expected result |
| --- | --- |
| Submit Cedar Trail Outfitters | Cedar Trail Outfitters; Located in: Fairhaven; CEO: Rowan Patel; Products offered: Daypack, Trail Bottle, Rain Shell |
| Submit Sunrise Bakery | Sunrise Bakery; Located in: Mapleton; CEO: Avery Kim; Products offered: Sourdough, Blueberry Muffin, Cinnamon Roll |
| Submit Harbor Books | Harbor Books; Located in: Lakeside; CEO: Morgan Reed; Products offered: Mystery Novel, Nature Guide, Sketchbook |
| Type Cedar and choose its autocomplete suggestion | The name is completed and the Cedar card appears with its local display image. |
| Submit a name with spaces around it | Surrounding spaces are ignored. |
| Submit No Such Business after a successful match | The previous card is hidden; No business found. is shown; no exception. |
| Submit an empty field or only spaces | Same no-match state. |
| Submit cedar trail outfitters | No match; the reference uses exact case-sensitive names. |
| Change a display_image to images/missing.svg and show that business | Image unavailable for followed by the business name; the other details remain usable. |
| Put HTML-looking text in a location/product string | The characters display as text. |
| Select two different businesses repeatedly | One current card and one current image/fallback, without old company details. |

The stock starter remains unfinished until its array and renderBusiness are
completed. For a browser check, complete it with the reference data and rendering,
then add a fourth fictional business and retain the earlier three.

reference.README.md:
# My Favorite Businesses II

Build a searchable business directory using arrays of objects, Materialize
autocomplete and D3 card rendering. This optional project extends My Favorite
Businesses. Its starter and reference are separate saved projects.

Open index.html directly in a browser without a server. The project includes
its libraries and example images; it works offline. Edit script.js.

## Required work

1. Copy at least three business objects from the earlier project. Keep each name,
   location, CEO and products array. Add logo_image and display_image to each.
   The included SVG files can be reused or replaced with local images.
2. Build autocomplete choices from the same array. The shared setup calls
   renderBusiness when a suggestion is chosen or Show business is submitted.
3. Complete renderBusiness. Trim surrounding spaces, find the exact name and
   render one Materialize card using the selected object's fields.
4. For blank/unknown names hide the previous card and show "No business found."
   Render values as text. Show a text fallback when the display image fails.

Materialize's onAutocomplete callback receives the chosen name. Its data option
maps names to logo URLs. D3 .text(value) writes text; .attr(name, null) removes an
attribute. Clear the old image container before inserting a new image so old
load/error events cannot change the new card.

The reference uses fictional Cedar Trail Outfitters, Sunrise Bakery and Harbor
Books. Reference matches are case sensitive; surrounding spaces are ignored.
Selecting a suggestion renders the card immediately. The Show business button
also accepts a typed exact name.

Read CASES.md for concrete inputs and expected results. Complete when all
businesses, autocomplete selection, repeated changes, unknown/blank names and
a broken image pass those checks. Save the project and export its ZIP.

The starter leaves the business array and rendering work unfinished. The
reference demonstrates one complete implementation.
reference.SOURCES.md:
# Sources and adaptation

Original assignment:
https://codepen.io/junilearning/pen/50854534e6dccd9c7bedc0a2d01aded7

Original reference:
https://codepen.io/junilearning/pen/7cbfe6e04babe21bb34a6d6af1028f57

Both complete original panels, all HTML/CSS/JS settings and official exports
were retained and compared on 2026-11-14. The original starter has blank HTML
and CSS and a comment brief. The reference uses Materialize 1.0.0 and D3 6.2.0
to search a three-company array and fill one card.

This local implementation supplies full HTML/CSS scaffolding, local example
images, a deliberately unfinished starter and a separate working reference.
Fictional records replace historical company facts. The no-match and failed-image
branches satisfy the site's existing assignment. The unnecessary legacy
jquery.materialize-autocomplete plug-in is omitted; Materialize's own
M.Autocomplete provides the assigned behavior.

D3 7.9.0 is the existing audited site adaptation, with the same selection/event
API used here. Materialize is the existing pinned 1.0.0 course asset. Libraries
and licenses are included. The original starter export's MIT notice is retained;
the official reference export contained no separate license file. The local
exercise implementation and SVG illustrations are newly authored.
